blocks.x: We’re living in an era where arguably the biggest crowd-pullers are not movie stars but a filmmaker and a fictional character. This summer saw both operating at the peak of their popularity. Spider-Man: Brand New Day, the fourth installment of the superhero series starring Tom Holland, grossed around $2.5 billion at the worldwide box office, despite signs that audiences had lost interest in the genre as a whole. Around the same time, Christopher Nolan delivered his biggest-ever hit, The Odyssey, which outgrossed previous films such as The Dark Knight and Oppenheimer. Remarkably, The Odyssey has almost doubled the global haul of Inception. The movie still hasn’t landed on the PVOD market, given Nolan’s strict theatrical exclusivity demands, but audiences can revisit one of his past hits this October on Netflix.

The movie in question was released in 2006, between Batman Begins and The Dark Knight. Nolan made a similar diversion before The Dark Knight Rises as well; this was when he directed Inception. The 2006 film reunited him with his Batman Begins star Christian Bale, who was joined by Hugh Jackman, Scarlett Johansson, and Rebecca Hall. The film is now considered one of his most underrated gems. Even though it was a solid box-office hit at the time, there’s a sense that it would’ve been much bigger had it been released now.

blocks.x: We’re talking, of course, about The Prestige, Nolan’s mind-bending thriller about dueling magicians in Victorian England. The film also features his frequent collaborator Michael Caine and a memorable supporting performance by David Bowie. It grossed $110 million worldwide against a reported budget of $40 million. It now holds a “Certified Fresh” 77% critics’ score and a 92% audience score on the aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, where the consensus reads, “Full of twists and turns, The Prestige is a dazzling period piece that never stops challenging the audience.” The movie was added to the Netflix library this October. Stay tuned to Collider for more updates.
